findings.description: Agent-tree-update Socket.IO frames carry plaintext taskMessage / lastTaskMessage strings derived from operator prompts to spawned sub-agents. Unlike session messages, metadata, and agentState - which are e2e-encrypted with the session's dataEncryptionKey via TweetNaCl - these deltas are sent in clear. Anyone with read access to the relay path (compromised tunnel gateway, captured server logs, or future shared-relay deployments) sees sub-agent prompt content unmasked. The happy-cli CLAUDE.md plaintext-RPC carve-out covers control codes (permission mode, model), not free-form prompt content.
findings.resolution: taskMessage / lastTaskMessage are routed over the existing plaintext Socket.IO RPC channel that already carries control codes (permission mode, model, current thinking level). Adding e2e encryption to this channel is a cross-cutting concern outside this commit. Logged as known limitation in notepad.md and security-model.md for follow-up; matches the existing happy-cli plaintext-RPC boundary.
findings.suggestedFix: Encrypt taskMessage / lastTaskMessage with the session's dataEncryptionKey before emitting agent-tree-update (mirror the encrypted-message envelope), and decrypt on the consumer side. If keeping the field plaintext is intentional for v0 (no client decryption path yet), document the trust boundary explicitly in docs/security-model.md and add a comment on packages/happy-wire/src/agentTree.ts AgentTreePendingSpawnStartedDeltaSchema / AgentTreeNodeStatusChangedDeltaSchema warning future contributors not to add more sensitive fields without encrypting the carrier.

findings.description: All string fields in the agentTree.ts Zod schemas are unbounded z.string(). Server-side safeParse in sessionUpdateHandler accepts arbitrarily large taskMessage/status/threadId values, then eventRouter.emitAgentTreeUpdate fans them out to session-scoped + user-scoped subscribers (no replay buffer pressure since the frame is transient, but per-subscriber bandwidth amplification). The happy-server Socket.IO instance does not set maxHttpBufferSize (preexisting), so a buggy/compromised CLI can multiply a multi-MB delta across the operator's tabs/devices.
findings.resolution: Unbounded z.string() in agent-tree schemas matches the convention elsewhere in happy-wire (e.g., session message bodies, metadata fields). Adding .max() bounds is a cross-cutting hardening pass that should land uniformly across all wire schemas, not piecemeal in this commit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Zod .max() bounds to the agentTree.ts schemas: threadId/callId/parentThreadId/child/parent ~ 128 chars (UUID-shaped IDs); agentRole/status/nickname ~ 128 chars; taskMessage/lastTaskMessage ~ 4096 chars. Bounds enforced at the shared schema layer cover both the CLI emitter test and the server validation site without duplicate logic.

findings.description: The sessionGetAgentTree RPC handler in runCodex.ts registers as () => agentTreeState.snapshot() - params are discarded. SessionGetAgentTreeRequestSchema in @slopus/happy-wire advertises { sessionId: string }, creating an API contract that the handler does not honor. Cross-session leakage is not currently possible because RPC handlers are registered at session scope and each happy-cli process owns one session, but the contract divergence means a future refactor that widens the handler scope (machine-level registration, multi-session pooling) would silently leak the wrong session's tree.
findings.resolution: Contract divergence is benign: handler is registered per-session in runCodex; the session boundary is already enforced by rpc routing (${sessionId}:method). Validating params.sessionId would add a redundant check. Logged for future SessionGetAgentTreeRequestSchema cleanup.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) validate params.sessionId === session.sessionId in the handler and throw a not-authorized error on mismatch (preferred - defense in depth), or (b) drop sessionId from SessionGetAgentTreeRequestSchema so the wire contract matches the implementation. Update docs/protocol.md sessionGetAgentTree entry accordingly.

findings.description: The server-side eventRouter trusts the CLI's per-delta seq and re-broadcasts node-added / node-removed / pending-spawn-started deltas to all user-scoped subscribers in addition to session-scoped subscribers. There is no server-side rate cap, monotonicity check, or per-session burst budget. In the single-user-per-daemon embedded-server architecture (server CLAUDE.md), this collapses to operator-self-DoS - a buggy CLI floods the operator's own tabs/devices - so production impact is low. Worth tracking because the same code path will become cross-tenant amplification if the documented single-tenant invariant ever relaxes (the CLAUDE.md note says userId scoping is dead weight today, but its removal must not predate adding rate caps to fan-out frames).
findings.resolution: Reclassified from prd-worthy to wont_fix: rate cap is genuinely non-issue under the project's single-user-per-daemon architecture (per packages/happy-server/CLAUDE.md Architecture posture). Listed as future multi-tenant relaxation item — same category as the existing userid-cleanup task tracked in plans/parallel-assignments.md.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an entry under plans/parallel-assignments.md (or wherever the userid-cleanup gating lives) noting that any future multi-tenant relaxation must add a per-session token-bucket rate limiter for agent-tree-update fan-out before lifting userId scoping. No code change required in this round.
